newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Playing drops in AMR, Bankamerica.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Playing drops in AMR, Bankamerica.

text.p: Options investors appeared to be taking advantage of options on shares of AMR Corp and BankAmerica Corp as the two stocks fell, traders said Friday.
Individual equity options activity was fairly scattered, with few clear strategies being played out in specific issues.

Shares of AMR were down ahead of a threatened strike by pilots at its American Airlines unit. The pilots are set to strike at midnight EST Friday (0500 GMT Saturday) unless they reach a contract agreement with company management.

Bankamerica, which closed Thursday at an all-time high, bucked a strong sector to decline in what traders said was profit-taking after a strong run. The stock goes ex-dividend on Tuesday, February 18.
AMR shares were down 1/2 at 82-5/8 on consolidated volume of about 695,000 shares. They reached a session low of 81-1/4.
AMR chief Robert Crandall said Thursday a 90-day strike could wipe out the company.
"The February 75, 80 and 85 puts are more active than normal," Michael Schwartz at Oppenheimer said. "A few people are just playing the downside possibility."
The AMR February 75 put traded 820 contracts, the February 80 put traded 830, and the February 85 put traded 175.

Open interest in each of those three options rose sharply Thursday, led by the 2,546 contracts that were opened in the February 75 put. That option also had the highest open interest of the three, with a total of 4,434 contracts.
The most active AMR call was the February 85, which traded 465 contracts. It had open interest of 1,030 contracts, which included 275 opened on Thursday.
The March 80 put and March 90 call also were busy.
For Bankamerica, traders said put buying was fairly heavy as the stock fell in heavy trade.
Bankamerica was down 2-3/4 at 120-1/4 on about 1.9 million shares in late activity. Traders said the stock was most likely down on profit-taking after Thursday's record close at 123.
"I haven't heard anything other than maybe taking some profits on it," one options trader said.
George Salem, an analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, noted Bankamerica shares have led the banking group. He said he was not aware of any news on it.
"Bankamerica has been a super strong stock," he said. "For it to retrace three points today is nothing at all."
The most active Bankamerica option was the February 110 call, which traded about 1,860 contracts.
But the February 115 put traded 1,750.
In the March series, the 110, 115 and 120 calls were fairly active, as were the 105 and 110 puts.
